description: Explains the east-west Pacific temperature gradient, thermocline tilt, Walker circulation, Bjerknes feedback, equatorial Kelvin waves, recharge and discharge, and why ENSO phases recur irregularly.

related_resources.reason: Pacific mean state, upwelling, Tahiti-Darwin pressure, coastal naming, warm/cool ENSO phases.
Original coupled Pacific SST/trade-wind/Southern Oscillation argument and remote winter circulation correlations.
Accumulated upper-ocean warm water, trade-wind relaxation and eastward Kelvin-wave hypothesis.
Recharge-discharge model with Bjerknes amplification and delayed oceanic heat-content response.
Mean Pacific state, upwelling, equatorial waves, warm-water volume, seasonality, nonlinearities and event diversity.

background: The lecture introduces ocean temperature, wind stress, convection and subsurface waves from first principles.
readiness_checks: How do trade winds help maintain a cool eastern Pacific?
How can a wind anomaly create further warming through atmospheric response?
Why can a subsurface Kelvin wave change the future of the sea surface?
